checks: For a nonempty family, finite-dimensional strict separation of the scaled all-ones vector from the finite convex hull gives a strict separator. Subtracting the stated multiple of w preserves its negative differences because each incidence vector has w-inner product M/k, and makes its coordinate sum zero. When the family is empty the strict conditions are vacuous.

Membership of the scaled all-ones vector in the convex hull gives a nonnegative cover by scaling by k. Any such cover has coefficient sum k by the inner product with w, and its dot product with a zero-total vector rules out simultaneous strict negativity.

For two same-label points, their midpoint is a point of P by hypothesis. The face property gives its incidence as the product of the endpoint incidences, including for the full face. Summing the nonnegative incidence discrepancies with the positive coefficients yields zero, so all three incidences agree in each active face.

Each label maps to one incidence class and every incidence class is hit. Coordinatewise coverage puts every incidence class inside at least one active face of mass alpha, so there are at most k classes, with total M=k alpha and each mass at most alpha. Equality forces a bijection and makes each class midpoint-closed. The closest-pair argument takes place in the finite-dimensional affine hull and works at every rank, with no pairs to check at rank zero.

The classes are singletons of mass alpha. Active faces contain exactly one such point, and a face of a finite convex hull is generated by the points it contains. Thus each covered atom is a vertex. Conversely, positivity and the equal weights make precisely the singleton vertices the mass-alpha faces, including the full face of a singleton. Each singleton coordinate forces its coefficient to be one.
